sources.title: United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNGA Res. 61/295)
sources.extract: Adopted 13 Sep 2007. Arts. 11(1) and 31(1): culture, designs and IP over them. Arts. 19 and 32(2): States seek consent through representative institutions. Art. 33(1): identity is the people's to determine. Arts. 19 and 32(2) address States.

sources.title: Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, SBC 2019, c. 44
sources.extract: Defines the Declaration as UNDRIP. s.3: government aligns BC laws with it in consultation with Indigenous peoples. s.4 action plan; ss.6-7 agreements. Binds government, not private designers. Litigation status: see S59, S60, S68.

sources.title: United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, S.C. 2021, c. 14
sources.extract: Royal Assent 21 Jun 2021. s.4 affirms the Declaration as a human-rights instrument with application in Canadian law; s.5 aligns federal laws; s.6 action plan with monitoring.

sources.title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada: Calls to Action
sources.publisher: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada
sources.extract: Call 92 asks the corporate sector to adopt UNDRIP: meaningful consultation and free, prior and informed consent before projects, equitable jobs and long-term benefits, staff education. Addressed to the corporate sector.

sources.title: City of Vancouver UNDRIP Strategy: Report of the UNDRIP Task Force (Council item P1, 25 Oct 2022)
sources.publisher: City of Vancouver with Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403 in rounds 0 and 1; City domains still blocked). Facts come from S06 and S07: 79 calls to action in four themes, endorsed by Council 25 Oct 2022.

sources.title: UNDRIP Task Force Celebrates Unveiling of Historic Report
sources.extract: Report released 19 Oct 2022 as the first co-developed UNDRIP strategy in Canada. Co-chairs Khelsilem and Christine Boyle. 79 calls to action, four themes. TWN councillors stress Coast Salish laws and revenue sharing.

sources.title: Vancouver City Council Passes Historic UNDRIP Strategy
sources.extract: Council passed the Strategy 25 Oct 2022; 79 actions across City departments. A committee of Host Nations, City and urban Indigenous representatives is to set what each action requires. Binding of non-City bodies not stated.

sources.title: City of Vancouver UNDRIP Action Plan 2024-2028
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403 again in r2; council.vancouver.ca copy also 403). Search summary only: endorsed 25 Jun 2024; 32 of 79 actions; 88 deliverables; annual reports since 2025. Verify in a browser.

sources.title: Musqueam Indian Band: Intergovernmental Affairs referral process
sources.extract: Addressed to proponents and regulators. Eight package items (project description, regulatory processes, studies, permits, correspondence, maps, GIS files, imagery). Fees not mentioned on the page (r2 re-read). No mention of student, academic or hypothetical projects.

sources.title: Musqueam Indian Band: Our Territory
sources.extract: Ancestors stewarded the Fraser River estuary for thousands of years. The 1976 Musqueam Declaration asserts title around the watershed draining into English Bay, Burrard Inlet and Indian Arm. Links the Place Names Map.

sources.title: Musqueam Place Names Map
sources.extract: Interactive map with Elder audio in hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓, photos and a children's book; says it is under review, not final. Requests go to a listed email; copyright is the Band's. r1 re-fetch failed (HTTP 520).

sources.title: Squamish Nation: Partnerships and Entities
sources.extract: Lists entities (Hiy̓ám̓ Housing, Nch'ḵay̓ Development Corporation, Squamish Nation Trust) and partnerships (MST, Sen̓áḵw, Cultural Centre) apart from the government. Hiy̓ám̓ orthography unresolved; no referral page.

sources.title: Tsleil-Waututh Nation Sacred Trust Initiative
sources.extract: Names Burrard Inlet səlilwət, a grandmother that sustained the Nation. TWN's assessment combined science and TWN knowledge and rests on its unextinguished law. Shows how the Nation frames its place.

sources.title: Sen̓áḵw (official project site, home and About pages)
sources.extract: Mountain Towers (curved, Coast Salish motifs, roofs angled to honour the Twin Sisters) and Long Towers (longhouse reference, salmon screens). Pool art by a Squamish artist. Net-zero claim is the developer's. No name meanings given.

sources.title: Sen̓áḵw (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: Kitsilano Indian Reserve No. 6, 11.7 acres. Settlement dated 2001 (lead) and June 2000 (History). Led by Nch'ḵay̓; Westbank exited to OPTrust Aug 2025. 6,000+ rentals; tallest 58 storeys. Height-exemption claim cites an unopened 2020 article.

sources.title: Dezeen: Revery Architecture's Sen̓áḵw towers
sources.extract: Revery is design architect, Kasian architect of record. 11+ towers of 12-58 storeys; village in the park; copper facades. Developer says Squamish members were consulted and a Cultural Working Group formed (developer statements).

sources.title: Jericho Lands policy statement approved by Vancouver council (Global News)
sources.extract: Council approved the policy statement 24 Jan 2024: about 13,000 homes, 4-49 storeys over 25-30 years. Partnership of MST Development Corporation and Canada Lands Company.

sources.title: Jericho Lands policy statement draft (Storeys)
sources.extract: Draft: heights peak at 26-39 storeys centrally; three Sentinel buildings for the three Nations rise to 49 storeys; podiums soften scale and protect views and sun. Draft stage.

sources.title: Policy Statement: Heather Lands
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403). Search summary: approved by Council 15 May 2018 at the request of the three Nations and Canada Lands Company; covers uses, density, height, form, parks.

sources.title: MST Development Corporation (About Us and Projects)
sources.extract: Partnership of Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh. Full or co-owner of six properties, 160+ developable acres; Jericho and Heather Street Lands co-owned with CLC. No design principles stated on these pages.

sources.title: CARE principles for Indigenous data (University of Auckland)
sources.extract: Four CARE principles: Collective benefit; Authority to control (Indigenous bodies decide how they and their lands are represented in data); Responsibility; Ethics.

sources.title: The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance (Carroll et al.), Data Science Journal 19(1):43
sources.extract: Authored with the Global Indigenous Data Alliance. CARE complements FAIR by adding people and purpose; informed by OCAP. Sub-principle wording not visible on the page opened.

sources.title: OCAP principles summary (University of Toronto Map and Data Library)
sources.extract: OCAP (1998): Ownership, Control, Access, Possession. Applied through each Nation's own laws, review committees and agreements.

sources.title: First Nations Information Governance Centre: OCAP
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403). Secondary sources say OCAP is an FNIGC registered trademark. Usage conditions unverified.

sources.title: Local Contexts: Traditional Knowledge (TK) Labels
sources.extract: TK Labels let communities state conditions: provenance (TK Attribution), protocol (TK Culturally Sensitive) and permission (TK Non-Commercial) labels. Icons and template text are copyrighted by Local Contexts.

sources.title: Local Contexts: Notices
sources.extract: Notices are applied by institutions and cannot be edited: Engagement, Disclosure (Attribution Incomplete, TK, Biocultural), Collections Care. Hub Agreements, API Guide and Terms not reviewed. Communities decide whether to add Labels.

sources.title: TCPS 2 (2022) Chapter 9: Research Involving the First Nations, Inuit and Metis Peoples of Canada
sources.publisher: Panel on Research Ethics (Government of Canada)
sources.extract: Art. 9.1: engage the community when research may affect its welfare, including cultural heritage. Art. 9.2: engagement form set jointly. Used by analogy for design, and directly if Indigenous people take part in tests or review.

sources.title: The International Indigenous Design Charter (ICoD news item)
sources.extract: Launched Montreal Oct 2017 on the Australian Indigenous Design Charter. Self-regulated, open, iterative; cited in an Australian inquiry. Lists no principles; its input claim is not supported by S49 (see flag).

sources.title: Indigenous Protocol and Artificial Intelligence Position Paper
sources.publisher: Indigenous Protocol and AI Working Group (hosted via Concordia University)
sources.extract: About 20 months of discussion among Indigenous participants from Aotearoa, Australia, North America and the Pacific. Warns of appropriation and extraction of traditional knowledge by data-hungry AI. Year unconfirmed.

sources.title: Native Land Digital: About
sources.extract: Maps are not official, do not define territories and treat borders as colonial; a starting point for conversation with communities. Nations define themselves.

sources.title: City of Vancouver Open Data: View cones (protected views)
sources.extract: API read r1 and cross-checked in r2 against S57 and S58: 24 records, Open Government Licence - Vancouver, no height field. Matches the 24 views kept on 10 Jul 2024; no removed id appears. Per-view pages return 403.

sources.title: City of Vancouver Open Data: Public art
sources.extract: Open Government Licence. 751 records; artists are numeric ids, no identity field. 17 mention Coast Salish. Records 738, 740, 741, 744: 2017 Canada 150+ murals by Indigenous artists, juried by an Indigenous panel. 738 is the former QE Theatre Plaza site.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge (Buildner competition page, FAQ and jury page)
sources.extract: r2 re-read: jury of seven (De Vries, Gill, Baker, Cheng, MacDougall, Lee, Soules of UBC SALA). Reg 29 Oct, Q&A 3 Nov, submit 30 Nov, winners 26 Jan 2027. Entries anonymous; no weights stated; brief linked, text not captured.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge official brief (facts as supplied in the project context)
sources.publisher: Buildner with City of Vancouver and UBC SALA
sources.extract: Brief PDF still NOT OPENED after two rounds (download link text not captured). Weights, criterion wording and site-plan facts come from the project context. Buildner page: site in the downtown core, no coordinates; lists site plans and a 3D model.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy (City of Vancouver, H005)
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403; Shape Your City copy did not render). City pages: established 1997, last reviewed 2011 (S67). Critic's search summary: amended to July 2018 and renamed; unverified.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy Review (review document, PDF)
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 403 again in r2). The review is described on the opened pages S66 and S67.

sources.title: IPTC NewsCodes: Digital Source Type vocabulary
sources.extract: r2 re-read: 20 concepts, several retired (digitalArt, softwareImage, minorHumanEdits). Active: trainedAlgorithmicMedia, compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia, algorithmicallyEnhanced, humanEdits, digitalCreation, compositeSynthetic, algorithmicMedia. Each has a stable URI.

sources.title: C2PA Technical Specification 2.3
sources.publisher: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
sources.extract: Supersedes 2.2; page says December 2025 (search result: 5 Jan 2026). Read: s14.2 one identity credential; s14.5 certificate chain in x5chain; claim_generator_info needs a name. Subject-field (O) rules not found in text read.

sources.title: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
sources.extract: Six outcomes: accountability, safety, fairness, transparency, human oversight, validity. Developers of public generative systems should provide detection such as watermarking. Launched Sept 2023.

sources.title: EU AI Act, Article 50: Transparency obligations (unofficial text site)
sources.extract: 50(2): providers mark synthetic output machine-readably; 50(4): deepfake disclosure, with an editorial-review exception for AI text. Provisional Omnibus deal 7 May 2026 reportedly moves 50(2) to 2 Dec 2026; adoption to be checked in the Official Journal. Benchmark only.

sources.title: PIPEDA fair information principles
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.extract: Ten principles including identifying purposes, consent, limiting collection, use, disclosure and retention, safeguards and openness.

sources.title: Personal Information Protection Act, SBC 2003, c. 63
sources.extract: Rules for private organizations handling personal information; consent generally required for collection, use or disclosure; business contact and work product excluded.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology (W3C Recommendation)
sources.extract: Published 30 Apr 2013. Core classes Entity, Activity, Agent; relations wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo exchange provenance as RDF.

sources.title: Mukurtu CMS: About
sources.publisher: Washington State University Center for Digital Scholarship and Curation
sources.extract: Open-source (GPL-3.0) platform for communities to manage digital heritage with cultural protocols as access levels and integrated TK Labels.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge: Competition Terms and Conditions
sources.extract: Fetch-tool summary; check clause numbers in a browser. 3.3.5 bars employees, contractors, associates of Organizer or Jury; 4.1 no prior publication; 5.1-5.3 anonymity, no approach to jurors or the undefined Commissioning Party; 8.3; 10.4 unnamed advisors; 10.10 Q&A; 12.3 authorship kept.

sources.title: Government of Canada guidance page on the Crown's duty to consult and accommodate (title not captured)
sources.publisher: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
sources.extract: The Crown holds the duty to consult; the page says it cannot be delegated, though proponents may do procedural tasks. Basis: Haida (2004), s.35. First 100,000 of 207,000 characters read.

sources.title: International Indigenous Design Charter: Protocols for sharing Indigenous knowledge in professional design practice (full book)
sources.publisher: Deakin University (hosted by the International Council of Design)
sources.extract: Ten protocols: Indigenous led; Self-determined; Community specific; Deep listening; Indigenous knowledge; Shared knowledge; Shared benefits; Impact of design; Legal and moral; Charter implementation. Copyright 2018, paraphrase only. Australian-led; no Coast Salish contributor; law prevails.

sources.title: Unicode Standard Annex 15: Unicode Normalization Forms
sources.extract: Unicode 18.0.0, revision 58, 2026-08-12. NFC is canonical decomposition then composition; normalising both strings lets a binary comparison decide equivalence.

sources.title: Content Authenticity Initiative: FAQ
sources.extract: Content Credentials can say who produced content, but identity is optional and sensitive information can be redacted later.

sources.title: Tsleil-Waututh Nation: Stewardship Work in the Territory (Treaty, Lands and Resources)
sources.extract: Describes research, policy and restoration work, mainly Burrard Inlet water quality; links industry and government guides (unread). No referral steps or named contact beyond the contact page.

sources.title: Tsleil-Waututh Nation: Language, Culture and Protocol Department
sources.extract: Gives cultural leadership and protocol support for Nation-led initiatives and partner projects; prioritises hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓. No outside-request process; only the contact form.

sources.title: Sen̓áḵw: City of Vancouver and Squamish Nation sign services agreement (Global News)
sources.extract: Signed 25 May 2022: City to provide water, utilities, electricity, fire and police services. The article says no City approvals are needed because it is Squamish land. Fees not mentioned (critic reports fees; unverified).

sources.title: Coast Salish names given to 2 Vancouver plazas (Salish Sea Sentinel)
sources.extract: 18 Jun 2018: QE Theatre plaza named šxʷƛ̓exən Xwtl'a7shn, Art Gallery north plaza šxʷƛ̓ənəq Xwtl'e7énḵ Square. A committee with Musqueam, Tsleil-Waututh and Squamish representatives chose the names; City Council decided. 'Gifted' absent. Strings as read by the fetch tool.

sources.title: Videos teach how to pronounce Indigenous-named plazas (Georgia Straight)
sources.extract: 18 Jun 2018: City and provincial officials with representatives of the three Nations renamed the plazas; names combine hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ and Sḵwx̱wú7mesh. Who chose the names and who holds rights to them not stated.

sources.title: Vancouver view cones policy change (Storeys)
sources.extract: 10 Jul 2024: Council repealed the view cones policy and adopted Public Views Guidelines. Of 38 cones, 14 removed, 11 amended, 24 remain. QE Park 3.2.1-3.2.4 kept; 3.1 and 3.2.4a removed.

sources.title: Vancouver city council removes view cones (Global News)
sources.extract: 11 Jul 2024: 14 view cones removed, 11 of the remaining 24 amended. Critics said public mountain views would shrink; supporters cited housing. Replacement guidelines not described.

sources.title: Supreme Court to hear appeal on UNDRIP's reach in domestic law (National Magazine)
sources.extract: SCC agreed to hear BC's appeal of the Gitxaała ruling (BCCA, Dec, 2-1). No hearing date or docket number given. Premier said government would amend DRIPA; no enacted amendment or suspension reported.

sources.title: Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, British Columbia (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: BCCA Dec 2025: DRIPA gives UNDRIP immediate legal effect in BC law. Apr 2026: Premier reversed a plan to amend DRIPA; joint working group for fall 2026. Aug 2026: Conservative petition to repeal. No suspension reported. Secondary.

sources.title: EU AI Act Omnibus deal: postponed deadlines and watermarking compromise (William Fry)
sources.extract: Provisional deal 7 May 2026: Art. 50(2) marking and related labelling duties from 2 Dec 2026 (four-month delay). Subject to formal endorsement; Official Journal publication expected before 2 Aug 2026, not confirmed.

sources.title: Can AI be an author? Federal Court asked to decide (Norton Rose Fulbright)
sources.extract: CIPO registered SURYAST in Dec 2021 naming an AI app as co-author. CIPPIC filed Federal Court application T-1717-24 in July 2024 to expunge it. Article dated Aug 2024; no ruling found.

sources.title: ISED consultation on copyright in the age of generative AI
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (HTTP 503). Named in the critique; URL not confirmed. Check status and any What We Heard report in a browser. Treated as unsettled.

sources.title: TCPS 2 (2022) Chapter 2: Scope and Approach (Art. 2.1, 2.5)
sources.publisher: Panel on Research Ethics (Government of Canada)
sources.extract: Art. 2.1: research with living participants, including course-based activities with a pedagogical purpose, needs REB review before it starts. Art. 2.5: testing within normal educational requirements, used only for assessment or improvement, is outside REB scope.

sources.title: UBC Office of Research Ethics: Student Researchers
sources.extract: Stand-alone student projects need ethics approval; course-based work is usually covered by one application from the instructor; above-minimal-risk projects need their own. Course-based guidelines (Jan 2026) not read.

sources.title: City of Vancouver: Higher Buildings Policy Review (Shape Your City page)
sources.extract: Policy established 1997. Phase 1 spring-summer 2026; draft policies fall 2026-winter 2027; adoption spring 2027. Protected public views will not be reviewed or updated. Names the City as competition host; non-entry ideas go to a City inbox.

sources.title: City of Vancouver: Higher Buildings Policy Review FAQs
sources.extract: Policy originally 1997, last reviewed and updated 2011, minor changes to upper limits since. Competition hosted by Buildner with the City and UBC SALA; it will not determine policy. Entrant use of the City inbox not addressed.

sources.title: Gitxaała v British Columbia (Chief Gold Commissioner), BC Court of Appeal decision
sources.extract: NOT OPENED (certificate error on a guessed path). Decision of Dec 2025, 2-1, as reported by S59 and S60. Citation unconfirmed; locate it at bccourts.ca.

flags.claim: Sen̓áḵw is an MST-led development (as framed in the packet scope).
flags.correction: Sen̓áḵw is a Squamish Nation project led by Nch'ḵay̓ Development Corporation on Kitsilano Indian Reserve No. 6, with OPTrust as 50% partner in Phases 1-2. MST leads Jericho Lands and Heather Lands with Canada Lands Company.
flags.detail: Sources S13, S15, S16, S18, S21. Case studies label tenure and decision authority separately, because a Nation-controlled reserve and a City-rezoned site are not comparable approval paths.

flags.claim: The International Indigenous Design Charter's principle list could not be retrieved, so M03 links rather than paraphrases (round 0 UNVERIFIED flag and M03 limits).
flags.correction: The full charter book is public and lists ten protocols: Indigenous led; Self-determined; Community specific; Deep listening; Indigenous knowledge; Shared knowledge; Shared benefits; Impact of design; Legal and moral; Charter implementation. M03 indexes cards to these names.
flags.detail: Copyright 2018 bars reproduction, so the tool names, links and paraphrases only. Protocol 1: Indigenous stakeholders oversee creative development. Verified from the saved PDF (S49) in r1.

flags.claim: The ICoD charter was built with input from Sami, Inuit, North American, Maori and Australian practitioners (S29 extract).
flags.correction: The appendix lists workshops in Australia, Denmark, Greenland and Sweden. The Montreal launch panel lists Canadian and US Indigenous panelists, including a Nisga'a architect. Maori appear only as designers of featured works. No Coast Salish contributor is named.
flags.detail: Evidence S49, appendix 4.2. Describe it as Australian-led with Nordic workshop input and a North American launch panel. Fit with Coast Salish protocol is unestablished and every charter card says so.

flags.claim: Referral-pack completeness against the Musqueam list is a verified metric for this entry (M01).
flags.correction: The page verifies a list of eight items, not that it applies to an ideas competition. It addresses proponents and regulators. The checklist leaves the entrant flow and stays as reference for real projects. Default is no contact.
flags.detail: S10 item 2 lists regulatory processes; the page mentions no academic or hypothetical projects. Many student requests would use Nation staff time without any land-use decision.

flags.claim: Personal-data fields at export = 0 is a verified threshold based on S34 and S35 (M07).
flags.correction: Status is team_assumption. The brief (S35) was not opened. The competition page confirms anonymous evaluation and the Terms bar identifying marks; neither states a file-metadata rule. A person must read the brief's anonymity clause.
flags.detail: Leak paths: handles and fork authors in provenance, the signer certificate chain a C2PA manifest carries (S39 s14.2, s14.5), and GPS or author fields in metadata.

flags.claim: Local Contexts Notices are Open to Collaborate, Attribution Incomplete, TK, BC and Collections Care (S27 round 0 extract).
flags.correction: The page lists an Engagement Notice, Disclosure Notices (Attribution Incomplete, Traditional Knowledge, Biocultural) and Collections Care Notices, and points to Hub Agreements, an API Guide and Terms. M05 reads Notice types from the Hub at run time; link-out until the terms are read.
flags.detail: Evidence: S27 re-read in r1.

flags.claim: The City view-cone dataset gives the full set of protected public views ('24 polygons of protected public views').
flags.correction: Treat the dataset as partial until it is checked against the City's view-protection guidelines in a browser. Zero intersections is not clearance. A touched cone still needs the City's per-view height rule.
flags.detail: r1 flag kept for the record. SUPERSEDED in r2: the 24 records match the retained set after the July 2024 Council decision (see the r2 view-cone flag).

flags.claim: The City view-cone dataset may be partial because view numbers 1-2, 4-8, 11-19, 23-26 and letters C, F, I are absent (r1 flag and M06 metric basis).
flags.correction: On 10 Jul 2024 Council removed 14 of 38 cones, amended 11 and left 24 under the new Public Views Guidelines. The 24 records match; no removed id (C1, C2.x, E1, E2.2, E3, F1.x, 12.1, 3.1, 3.2.4a, 9.2.2, 20.2) appears.
flags.detail: S57, S58, S32 cross-checked in r2. Why whole numbers are absent is not stated in sources opened. Zero intersections is still not clearance: no heights in the data; guidelines not opened.

flags.claim: The governing document is the 'Higher Buildings Policy for Rezonings (1997)' and whether it was amended is unverified (S36).
flags.correction: City pages call it the Higher Buildings Policy: established 1997, last reviewed and updated 2011, minor upper-limit changes since, under review 2026-27. Protected views are not part of the review.
flags.detail: S66, S67. The critic's amendment to July 2018 and renaming come from a search summary; H005 returned 403. Status shown as current, under review; 2018 amendment unverified.

flags.claim: No source describes a services agreement between Sen̓áḵw and the City (r1 flag; M04 field marked unverified).
flags.correction: The City and Squamish Nation signed a services agreement on 25 May 2022 for water, utilities, electricity, fire and police services. Tenure: reserve land; City services by agreement; no City land-use approvals needed.
flags.detail: S54 (Global News). Fees are not in that article; the City release is unopened. The Wikipedia height-exemption claim is replaced by this sourced fact.

flags.claim: A downtown plaza naming precedent could not be found; the critic's Art Gallery example is unverified (r1 flag).
flags.correction: On 18 Jun 2018 the QE Theatre plaza and the Art Gallery north plaza received names combining hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ and Sḵwx̱wú7mesh. A committee with representatives of the three Nations chose them; the City renamed them.
flags.detail: S55, S56. Reports say 'given' and 'chosen', never 'gifted'. Sources differ on the Province's role. Rights to the names not stated. A person must re-copy the strings and check NFC.

flags.claim: EU AI Act Article 50 applies from 2 Aug 2026 (S42 extract).
flags.correction: A provisional Omnibus deal of 7 May 2026 reportedly moves the Art. 50(2) marking duty to 2 Dec 2026. Check formal adoption in the Official Journal. Benchmark only; not binding in BC.
flags.detail: S61. Adoption was expected before 2 Aug 2026 but is not confirmed here. The tool shows no EU date to users.

flags.claim: The Q&A route closes 3 Nov 2026 and can settle whether a Nation-contact channel exists (M01 method, UNRESOLVED flag).
flags.correction: Cl. 10.10: one free question per registration, due three days after registration closes (1 Nov unless the portal says otherwise), and only the five most-voted reach the jury. An answer is not assured; N0 is the standing default.
flags.detail: S47 (fetch-tool summary; browser check needed). Registration closes 29 Oct, so asking needs registration first. The page shows 3 Nov; the tool shows both dates.

flags.claim: Contacting the one Coast Salish juror and her firm is the juror-contact risk (M01 contact_guard).
flags.correction: Cl. 5.2 bars approaching any of seven jurors or the undefined Commissioning Party; cl. 8.3 voids prizes. The jury includes UBC SALA's Matthew Soules. The guard covers all seven jurors and firms, the Commissioning Party and Buildner's advisors.
flags.detail: S34, S47. SALA desk crits from him are a risk for UBC entrants. The City page names the City as host; the FAQ names Buildner with the City and SALA.

flags.claim: Canadian Indigenous design charters published by Nations or Indigenous design bodies exist for tall-building design.
flags.correction: None found for tall buildings or Coast Salish territory. The closest instrument is the International Indigenous Design Charter (S49), which is Australian-led.
flags.detail: No Nation-published design guideline for downtown towers was found in r1 or r2.

flags.claim: City of Vancouver policy documents (UNDRIP Strategy PDF, Action Plan 2024-2028, Higher Buildings Policy PDF and review PDF, Heather Lands statement, per-view pages) say what the packet summarises.
flags.detail: vancouver.ca, guidelines and syc domains returned 403 again in r2; shapeyourcity.ca opened (S66, S67). The 32-of-79 figure and the Heather date come from search summaries. A teammate must open these in a browser.

flags.claim: The Higher Buildings Policy was amended in July 2018 and renamed from 'General Policy for Higher Buildings' (critic, via search summary).
flags.detail: Not seen in S66 or S67, which say established 1997, reviewed 2011, minor upper-limit changes since. H005 returned 403. M02 shows the amendment as unverified until a person opens the PDF.

flags.claim: City view cones carry height limits the tool can read.
flags.detail: The dataset has no height field. Permitted heights sit in the Public Views Guidelines (2024), which could not be opened. Whether QE Park views set downtown height caps is unverified. Plan intersection is only a trigger to check.

flags.claim: OCAP can be named, badged or implemented as a compliance label in the tool.
flags.detail: Secondary sources say OCAP is an FNIGC registered trademark; FNIGC pages returned 403. Do not display OCAP-compliant; cite OCAP only as principles with a link.

flags.claim: Sen̓áḵw developer statements (consultation process, net-zero claim, below-market rents) are established facts.
flags.detail: They are the project's or developer's statements (senakw.com, Dezeen). Show them as stated, with an as-of date. S16 gives two settlement dates (2001, June 2000). Wikipedia's height-exemption claim cites an unopened 2020 article.

flags.claim: BC Sans or another open font covers every codepoint in the Nation-name registry.
flags.detail: BC Sans README says modified Noto Sans with BC Indigenous-language support; no characters named, licence unread. Gentium is OFL-1.1; First Nations orthographies unconfirmed. M05 and M07 test coverage per string.

flags.claim: The signing certificate in a C2PA manifest identifies the team or an individual, or a signer organisation (CAI docs per critic).
flags.detail: C2PA 2.3 requires the certificate chain (s14.5) and a claim_generator_info name; subject-field rules were not found in the text read. Rule: credentials off in competition mode; if on, neutral organisation and generic text.

flags.claim: In April 2026 the BC government proposed suspending key DRIPA sections (critic).
flags.detail: Not found. S60 reports the Premier reversed a plan to amend DRIPA in April 2026 and set a working group; S59 reports SCC leave. Outcome of both unverified; check BC Legislature and news.gov.bc.ca.

flags.claim: Canadian copyright treatment of AI-assisted images is settled enough for the tool to state ownership.
flags.detail: It is not. The SURYAST registration is challenged in CIPPIC v. Sahni (T-1717-24, filed July 2024; no ruling found, S62). The ISED consultation (S63) is unopened. The tool never states copyright status.

flags.claim: Zero-tolerance gates (no wording above declared status, no unresolved cultural-content flags, no missing AI labels, no identity-bearing fields on export).

case_studies.tool: Local Contexts (TK Labels, BC Labels, Notices, Hub)
case_studies.what_it_does: Lets Indigenous communities attach conditions to cultural material (Labels) and lets institutions flag Indigenous interests (Notices: Engagement, Disclosure, Collections Care).
case_studies.workflow_step: Provenance and permission of any Indigenous-derived asset (M05)
case_studies.how_used: Tool shows Notices and community Labels read-only, pulling Notice types from the Hub at run time; link-out only until Hub terms are read.
case_studies.strengths: Community-controlled; Notice text cannot be changed; widely adopted in archives.
case_studies.stops_at: Cannot decide whether a use is permitted; the tool cannot assign Labels for a community.
case_studies.license_cost: Icons and template text copyrighted by Local Contexts; Hub terms and API guide not reviewed.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Prompt when an asset is tagged cultural but has no Hub record.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Deciding who holds authority over knowledge or whether permission is real.

case_studies.what_it_does: Open-source platform where communities set cultural protocols as access levels, with TK Labels built in.
case_studies.workflow_step: Reference pattern for protocol-based access in M05
case_studies.how_used: Pattern only: Nation-held material stays in Nation-controlled systems and is linked, not copied.
case_studies.strengths: Designed with Indigenous communities; protocols are first-class.
case_studies.stops_at: A heritage-management system, not a design tool; GPL-3.0 would impose copyleft if embedded.

case_studies.what_it_does: Indigenous-led map of territories, treaties and languages as a starting point for conversation.
case_studies.how_used: Link-out only; the tool never draws territory boundaries as authoritative.
case_studies.strengths: Accessible entry point; states it is not an official source.
case_studies.stops_at: Not authoritative, not a consultation tool, does not define territories.
case_studies.license_cost: API and licence terms not stated on the page opened; unverified.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Which Nation to approach and how.

case_studies.what_it_does: Nation-run interactive map with Elder audio in hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓, photos and a children's book.
case_studies.workflow_step: Place-name and language strings (M01 stage B, M05)
case_studies.how_used: Link-out and a prompt to contact the Nation; strings are never scraped or machine-translated.
case_studies.strengths: Nation-authored and authoritative for what it covers.
case_studies.stops_at: Marked under review, not final; no stated citation or reuse rules.
case_studies.license_cost: Site copyright held by the Band; no reuse permission stated.

case_studies.tool: C2PA Content Credentials with IPTC Digital Source Type
case_studies.what_it_does: Open standard for signed provenance records, plus a vocabulary for marking images as AI-generated or AI-edited.
case_studies.workflow_step: Labelling AI output on boards and exports (M07)
case_studies.how_used: Embed the mapped IPTC term and a visible label on AI-involved export images. Credentials off in competition mode; if on, neutral organisation and generic claim-generator text, both listed in the metadata panel.
case_studies.strengths: Open specification (2.3); open-source SDK; identity optional.
case_studies.stops_at: Labels are declared and easily stripped; they do not prove authorship or permission; a certificate chain and claim-generator name travel with every manifest.
case_studies.license_cost: c2pa-rs MIT OR Apache-2.0; spec 2.3 licence not confirmed; certificates may cost money (unverified).
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Auto-fill labels from the tool's own generation log.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Whether using AI for a given element is appropriate.

case_studies.tool: City of Vancouver Open Data: View cones
case_studies.what_it_does: 24 polygons of protected public views, including Queen Elizabeth Park views 3.2.1 to 3.2.4, with links to per-view pages.
case_studies.how_used: Plan-intersection of the georeferenced massing with the polygons; lists touched cones with links, each a rule a person must check in the Public Views Guidelines.
case_studies.strengths: Official, open licence, API; 24 records match the set kept on 10 Jul 2024.
case_studies.stops_at: No height field; zero intersections is not clearance; guidelines not opened.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Extract permitted heights from the guidelines for a human to check, once they can be opened.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Judgement on whether a view loss is acceptable.

case_studies.tool: International Indigenous Design Charter (ICoD / Deakin University)
case_studies.what_it_does: Self-regulated guide with ten protocols for designers and buyers working with Indigenous knowledge.
case_studies.workflow_step: Prompt-card deck and expression-channel locks (M03, post-competition)
case_studies.how_used: Cards named after the ten protocols, one-line paraphrases, linked; no reproduction.
case_studies.strengths: Names Indigenous-led process, shared benefits and legal and moral permissions; backed by an international design body.
case_studies.stops_at: Australian-led; no Coast Salish contributor; not a Nation's own rule; territorial law prevails.
case_studies.license_cost: Copyright 2018; reproduction barred; free to read.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Match declared elements to the protocol they touch.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Whether a Coast Salish custodian would accept the design.

case_studies.tool: City of Vancouver Open Data: Public art registry (Canada 150+ Indigenous murals)
case_studies.what_it_does: Open registry of public artworks; records 738, 740, 741 and 744 are 2017 murals by Indigenous artists on downtown sites.
case_studies.how_used: Shows how City-owned downtown sites commissioned Indigenous artists and that several works are removed; the plaza naming process comes from S55 and S56.
case_studies.strengths: Official, open licence, API, commissioning statements.
case_studies.stops_at: Artist names are numeric ids; no identity field; the record does not say who named the plaza.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Whether a precedent's process can be copied.

case_studies.tool: Unicode normalization (UAX 15) with OFL fonts (BC Sans, Gentium)
case_studies.what_it_does: Makes canonically equivalent strings compare equal and lets PDFs show combining marks in hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ and Sḵwx̱wú7mesh sníchim.
case_studies.workflow_step: Name-string registry (M05) and export glyph check (M07)
case_studies.how_used: Store Nation-sourced strings in NFC; compare after normalization; embed fonts; fail export if a codepoint has no glyph.
case_studies.strengths: Standard and free; BC Sans described as Noto Sans with BC Indigenous-language support; Gentium is OFL-1.1.
case_studies.stops_at: Normalization does not fix wrong orthography; coverage and mark placement are untested.
case_studies.license_cost: Gentium OFL-1.1; BC Sans licence not read.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Flag strings that fail normalization or lack glyphs.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Spelling, meaning or permitted use of any string.

modules.name: Per-Nation engagement ledger, claims lint, contact guard and eligibility check
modules.design_question: What can this entry truthfully say about engagement with each Nation, whom must entrants not contact, and is the team eligible?
modules.effort: Stage A 3 person-days (N0 statement, full contact guard, eligibility check, ban-list lint; unreviewed beta); stage B 3 more after Indigenous review
depends_on: review_state manifest flag (set in M08 register; no runtime dependency)
inputs: Project metadata: site, competition entry flag
Per-Nation declared status, counterpart type, evidence note
Organizer Q&A log (question, date, pasted answer)
Board and narrative text from PRES nodes
Eligibility answers (private)
Nation-name registry from M05 (stage B)
outputs: engagement_ledger.json (per Nation: status, counterpart, date, declared-by, evidence, authorization reference)
claims_lint_report (phrase, location, Nation, minimum status, pass/fail)
contact_guard_card (seven jurors, Commissioning Party, advisors, acknowledged flag)

parameters.name: engagement_status_per_nation
parameters.unit: enum per Nation (Musqueam, Squamish, Tsleil-Waututh): N0 no contact (default); N1 desk research only (not engagement); N2 organizer Q&A answer logged (not engagement); N3 conversation with a person, counterpart recorded; N4 written permission from an authorized decision-maker for one stated use
parameters.relationship: Higher status permits stronger wording for that Nation only. N1 allows wording that names the documents read, never engagement wording. One Nation's status says nothing about the other two.

parameters.name: counterpart_type
parameters.unit: enum: community member, Indigenous artist or consultant, Nation staff, authorized Nation representative, Nation-owned corporation
parameters.relationship: Only a written decision from an authorized representative supports approved-by wording; other types support only spoke-with wording. Team design; the Indigenous reviewer sets the final list.

parameters.name: claim_vocabulary
parameters.unit: phrase list mapped to minimum status and counterpart
parameters.relationship: Duty-sense 'consulted' is banned for every entry: the duty sits with the Crown. Approved-by or endorsed-by needs an authorized-decision reference. 'In collaboration with', 'co-designed', 'with the blessing of' and 'honouring ... with permission' are banned for N0-N3.

parameters.name: juror_and_firm_list
parameters.unit: De Vries (MVRDV); Gill (AS+GG); Baker (K̓ESU+CO); Cheng (James K.M. Cheng Architects); MacDougall (Focal Engineering); Lee (PWL Partnership); Soules (Matthew Soules Architecture, UBC SALA)
parameters.relationship: Naming every juror and firm lets entrants avoid contact by name, including no feedback on the entry from Soules or in SALA reviews he attends. Copied from the jury page; rechecked at each release.

parameters.name: contact_guard
parameters.unit: fixed card plus acknowledgement flag, required before any export
parameters.relationship: Cl. 5.2 bars approaching any juror or the Commissioning Party; cl. 8.3 voids prizes. Buildner's cultural, budget and technical advisors (cl. 10.4) are unnamed; entrants must not seek them out. Questions go through the portal only.

parameters.name: commissioning_party_rule
parameters.unit: text rule plus a question for Buildner
parameters.relationship: The Terms never define Commissioning Party. The City page names the City as host; the FAQ names Buildner with the City and UBC SALA. Entrants use published City documents only and never contact City staff about the entry.

parameters.name: eligibility_self_check
parameters.unit: yes/no card quoting cl. 3.3.5; private record
parameters.relationship: Cl. 3.3.5 bars employees, interns, contractors and associates or family of the Organizer or Jury; 'associate' is undefined. Uncertain cases go to Buildner staff, never a juror. Authors record their own status in the README.

parameters.name: qa_route
parameters.unit: dates and counts shown on the card
parameters.relationship: Cl. 10.10: one free question per registration, due three days after the 29 Oct close (1 Nov unless the portal says otherwise; page says 3 Nov); only the top five voted reach the jury. N0 stays the standing default.

parameters.name: referral_reference_items
parameters.unit: count 0-8, reference only, real-project mode
parameters.relationship: Musqueam's eight items describe a real project with regulatory permits. They never prompt an entrant to send a referral, because applicability to competition entries is not established.

parameters.name: nation_name_strings
parameters.unit: NFC strings with source URL, retrieval date, codepoints (stage B)
parameters.relationship: Names copied from each Nation's own page keep the Nation in charge of how it is named; typed or machine-translated strings misrepresent people and places. Equivalent sequences must match after normalization.

metrics.name: Wording above declared status, per Nation
metrics.basis: Platform rule: consent and consultation are decided by Nations and governments, so claims of them must be true. Lint checks wording only.
metrics.method: Phrase lint of board text against each Nation's declared status.

metrics.name: Banned or unsupported phrases (duty-sense consulted; unreferenced approved or endorsed; collaboration phrases at N0-N3)
metrics.basis: The duty to consult cannot be delegated; UNDRIP Arts. 19 and 32(2) address States. Collaboration wording can read as engagement. Zero is a platform rule; list unreviewed.
metrics.method: Fixed ban list in stage A; extended list after review.

metrics.name: Per-Nation status and evidence note declared at export
metrics.good: yes for all three, with evidence note for N2-N4
metrics.basis: Course rule: every result shows its work.
metrics.method: Check ledger exists and is complete.

metrics.name: Contact guard acknowledged (all seven jurors and firms, Commissioning Party, advisors)
metrics.bad: no, or guard lists fewer than seven jurors
metrics.basis: r1 guard named one juror. Cl. 5.2 and 8.3 cover all jurors and the Commissioning Party, including UBC SALA's Soules. Acknowledgement is a platform rule.
metrics.method: Check the guard text and the flag before export.

metrics.name: Eligibility self-check completed before export
metrics.basis: Cl. 3.3.5 excludes associates of the Organizer or Jury; ineligibility could void an entry. Platform rule to prompt the check.
metrics.method: Check the private record exists.

metrics.name: Nation-channel question: both dates shown and N0 stated as standing default
metrics.bad: 3 Nov shown alone, or a sanctioned channel implied
metrics.basis: r1 treated the Q&A as able to settle the question by 3 Nov. Cl. 10.10 sets 1 Nov by default, one free question, top-five vote.
metrics.method: Check card text.

metrics.name: Referral-pack completeness (Musqueam list)
metrics.good: Not applicable to competition entries; real projects only
metrics.bad: Entrant flow prompts, counts or scores completeness
metrics.basis: Round 0 marked 8 of 8 verified. The page verifies the list, not that it applies to an ideas competition.
metrics.method: Checklist rendered only in real-project mode.

metrics.name: Indigenous-language strings with Nation source and NFC form (stage B)

modules.method: A YAML deck. Ten starter cards are indexed to the charter's ten protocols, each paraphrased in one line and linked, because the book bars reproduction; four team cards cover benefit, place names, what the team will not do, and a static do-not-derive-form-from card. Each card has a prompt, a source badge, a what-the-tool-can-check line and a what-only-people-or-Nations-can-answer line. Users choose one of four states: not considered, considering, responded with evidence, needs Nation input. The channel selector locks form, naming, pattern and commissioned art unless the status for that Nation is N4 for that use. Provenance cards call M05; land, water and view cards call M06. The deck is gated by review_state and is not part of the VTC 2026 entrant product. No numeric aggregation.

modules.human_judgment: All of it: which principles apply, how to read them, what to change in the design, and when to stop and ask the Nations. The tool only prompts and records.
modules.limits: No Nation-published guideline for tall buildings was found. The charter is Australian-led and self-regulated; no Coast Salish contributor is named; territorial law prevails. Cards are prompts, not approvals, and say so. Unreviewed until sign-off.

modules.method: 1) Every asset, including reference images, enters a manifest with hash, source URL, licence, author, AI-use field and declared authorship. 2) A human sets the cultural-content flag; keyword assist only suggests. 3) A flagged asset needs a permission record before the gate turns green. 4) AI prompts and reference images are checked against an editable, advisor-curated term list; Indigenous motif, pattern or sacred-image generation is refused with a clause link and logged. 5) Board text is scanned for borrowed-form phrases; hits are amber for review. 6) Nation-held layers are stored as URL plus retrieval date, never cached. 7) Registry strings are stored in NFC and glyph-checked. 8) Notices and Labels from a Hub project ID show read-only once Hub terms are read. modules.name: City in Nature and skyline identity prompts with georeferenced view geometry
modules.design_question: Where is the block, what does the design do for public views to mountains and water, and how are skyline, nature and local materials shown, not asserted?
modules.effort: Georeference and geometry outputs 2 person-days (core); view ray casting 5 days (may slip to v1); cultural prompt cards gated until review
depends_on: review_state manifest flag (cards and Nation names)
inputs: Layer 0 tower geometry, heights, public-space tags
Site boundary, labelled directions on the VTC site plan (rotated north arrow; from supplied summary until brief opened) and the user's georeference
Context massing: existing and approved towers (SITE)
City view-cone polygons (open data)
User-placed viewpoints tagged public or private amenity
Declared materials with origin, planting palette, water features

parameters.name: site_georeference
parameters.unit: lat/lon of a block corner, grid rotation in degrees, source (brief or team assumption)
parameters.relationship: The block is hypothetical but cone polygons and bearings are real. Placement decides which cones the massing touches and which bearings apply, so cone and azimuth outputs stay blocked until it is set and printed on every output.

parameters.name: viewpoint_set
parameters.unit: points (x, y, eye height) tagged public or private amenity
parameters.relationship: Public-realm points carry the City in Nature and view-protection argument; terraces and typical floors are private amenity views, reported separately. Higher points see more azimuth; ground points depend on podium height and tower spacing.

parameters.name: target_bearing_ranges
parameters.unit: degrees from site-plan labels
parameters.relationship: The brief's north arrow is rotated against the street grid, so bearings come from the labelled directions (Stanley Park, BC Place, Entertainment District, Burrard Inlet, North Shore Mountains); assuming true north reports views toward the wrong landmark.

parameters.name: obstruction_context
parameters.unit: set of existing and approved towers
parameters.relationship: More approved towers in the same height range narrow the unobstructed azimuth at public-realm viewpoints, so tower spacing and orientation change the views public space keeps.

parameters.name: tower_face_width_toward_viewpoint
parameters.unit: m and degrees subtended
parameters.relationship: A wider face toward the Queen Elizabeth Park bearing subtends a larger angle in the skyline view; a slimmer face or rotation subtends less. Geometry, not a cultural claim.

parameters.name: view_cone_intersection
parameters.unit: which of the 24 dataset cones the massing intersects in plan
parameters.relationship: The 24 records match the views kept under the Public Views Guidelines (2024). Development inside a polygon is height-limited, so an intersection means the guideline rule for that view must be checked. No heights are in the data, so zero intersections is not clearance.

parameters.name: place_and_feature_names
parameters.unit: City name from City data; Nation name only after review_state release; each with source; never translated
parameters.relationship: Until Indigenous sign-off M06 shows City names and geometry only. After release, Nation and City names appear side by side, keeping naming authority with their sources; no cultural meaning is derived from a direction.

parameters.name: cultural_prompt_cards
parameters.unit: skyline-identity and Nation-view cards, gated by review_state
parameters.relationship: Cards that mention Nations, Indigenous meaning or cultural identity are cultural content: hidden from entrants until reviewed, so unreviewed prompts do not shape entries. City in Nature and material-origin prompts stay open.

parameters.name: material_origin_and_nature_declaration
parameters.unit: free text with source
parameters.relationship: A declared origin and an evidence link turn local material and City in Nature from adjectives into checkable statements; no sourced numeric threshold was found. A cultural claim about a material is locked by M03 below N4.

modules.name: Ethical AI, authorship and anonymity-safe provenance ledger with competition-project mode
modules.design_question: Can every result, image and sentence show who or what made it, what each person decided, and from which sources, while a competition entry stays private and a competition export carries no identifying information?
modules.effort: 9 person-days (core: competition-project mode, identity stripping, AI label and source-id lint first)
depends_on: Platform project-sharing, fork, gallery and search settings (platform packet)
inputs: Every node output (metrics, images, text)
Asset manifest (owned here; read by M05)
Contributor handles (pseudonymous, platform mode only)
AI-tool log: model, version, prompt hash, date, tool terms link
Per-element human_contribution and decided_by entries
Module licences and source ids
Registry strings and export fonts (from M05)
outputs: provenance.jsonld (entities, activities, agents, human_contribution, decided_by; private)
board_appendix.md (AI use, sources, module names and licences only)
export_checklist (shows contribution and decision records; not printed on boards)

parameters.name: competition_project_mode
parameters.unit: on by default when the VTC entry flag is set: private, no forks, no gallery or search listing, handles hidden until 26 Jan 2027
parameters.relationship: A project, fork graph or gallery image visible before results can link an entry to its authors (cl. 5.1, 5.3) and count as previous publication (cl. 4.1). Private, unforkable, unlisted projects keep the entry unpublished and anonymous.

parameters.name: public_sharing_block
parameters.unit: warn-and-block on any public share of a board image before results
parameters.relationship: A public post of a board image can break cl. 4.1 and de-anonymise the team. Blocking and warning keeps entry images unpublished until 26 Jan 2027; the organizer judges any violation.

parameters.name: ai_involvement
parameters.unit: enum none, assistive edit, composite, generated
parameters.relationship: Declared level sets the visible label and IPTC term: none to humanEdits or digitalCreation; assistive edit to algorithmicallyEnhanced; composite to compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia; generated to trainedAlgorithmicMedia (team mapping). Under-declaring breaks trust.

parameters.name: human_contribution
parameters.unit: enum per element: concept, selection, edit, none
parameters.relationship: Records what a person contributed to each element. AI authorship law is unsettled and the Terms require original work, so the record shows the team's actual role. Shown in the export checklist, not on boards.

parameters.name: decided_by
parameters.unit: enum per decision: code, AI, person
parameters.relationship: Course rule: separate what code, AI and people decide. Stored in the PROV record so the export checklist shows who decided each element and nothing is credited to a person who did not decide it.

parameters.name: authorship_status_rule
parameters.unit: fixed rule: the tool never states copyright or ownership status
parameters.relationship: CIPO registered an AI co-author (SURYAST); CIPPIC's July 2024 application to expunge is pending; ISED consulted on AI and copyright. Terms cl. 12.3 keep authorship with the participant. The tool records contributions only.

parameters.name: contributor_identity_mode
parameters.unit: enum platform mode (handles and fork authors kept) or competition-export mode (all removed)
parameters.relationship: Handles give attribution on the platform. For export every handle, fork author and author field is removed from boards, appendix and file metadata, because the Terms bar marks identifying the author's source.

parameters.name: content_credentials_mode
parameters.unit: enum off (default, forced off in competition mode), platform-signed, user-signed
parameters.relationship: A C2PA manifest carries the signer certificate chain and a claim-generator name, so a SALA-identifiable signer could signal origin. If on outside competition mode, use a neutral organisation name and generic claim-generator text, both listed in the metadata panel.

parameters.name: tool_content_badge
parameters.unit: badge on every tool-authored card or list: AI-drafted, human-checked (who and when, platform-side)
parameters.relationship: The platform's own card paraphrases, crosswalk summaries and phrase lists are drafted by AI research agents through a summarising fetch tool. The badge tells users which content a person has checked.

parameters.name: human_review_of_ai_text
parameters.unit: named reviewer (platform record), date; board AI-text label rule
parameters.relationship: AI-drafted board text is declared in the appendix with its extent (drafted or edited); AI-drafted cultural text needs a named reviewer. EU Art. 50(4) review exception and the Canadian code's human oversight are benchmarks. Reviewer's name stays off export.

parameters.name: source_citation_completeness
parameters.unit: share of results with source ids
parameters.relationship: A result without a source id cannot be checked, so it shows as unsourced and its thresholds turn into editable team assumptions.

parameters.name: module_licence_and_attribution_chain
parameters.unit: SPDX id and upstream links
parameters.relationship: A forked module inherits upstream attribution; an incompatible licence raises a merge warning. The appendix lists module names and licences only, not authors. SPDX list not opened.

parameters.name: image_licence_record
parameters.unit: per image: licence or AI-tool terms link, date
parameters.relationship: The Terms require originality and non-infringement and let the organizer ask for image licences; Buildner tells entrants to check AI tools' terms. A per-image record lets the team answer quickly.

parameters.name: export_glyph_coverage
parameters.unit: codepoints with a glyph in the embedded fonts
parameters.relationship: Nation-language strings use combining marks. If an embedded font lacks a glyph, the PDF shows a box or a substitute, which misrepresents the name on the board.

metrics.name: Entry assets publicly reachable before results (project page, fork graph, gallery, search, shared board images)
metrics.basis: Platform rule backed by Terms cl. 4.1 (no previously published visual materials), 5.1 and 5.3 (anonymity until winners are chosen). Whether a private page counts as published is the organizer's call.
metrics.method: Check project visibility, fork graph, gallery and search index; a person checks social posts.

metrics.name: Results or claims without a source id
metrics.basis: Course rule: every result cites its source.
metrics.method: Scan provenance graph.

metrics.name: Elements without human_contribution and decided_by records
metrics.basis: Course rule: separate what code, AI and people decide; AI authorship law is unsettled.
metrics.method: Scan PROV records for the two fields.

metrics.name: AI-involved images without both a visible label and an embedded digital source type
metrics.basis: IPTC gives the terms; the Canadian code expects transparency; EU Art. 50(2) is a benchmark only and reportedly applies from 2 Dec 2026, not 2 Aug 2026.
metrics.method: Check metadata and overlay per image.

metrics.name: Identity-bearing fields in competition export (author, creator, handle, fork author, signer certificate or organisation, GPS, claim-generator string)
metrics.basis: Round 0 marked this verified. The brief was not opened and the Terms state no metadata rule. Handles, fork authors and C2PA signer data are additional leak paths.
metrics.method: Strip, then scan files for author, creator, name, email, handle, certificate and GPS fields; a person reads the brief's anonymity clause.

metrics.name: Tool-authored cards or lists without a provenance badge
metrics.basis: Course rule: show who drafted and who checked; platform content is AI-drafted.
metrics.method: Scan card and list manifests.

metrics.name: Team assumptions shown without the editable-assumption flag
metrics.basis: Platform rule: unsourced thresholds are visible as editable team assumptions.
metrics.method: Compare thresholds with source ids.

metrics.name: AI-drafted cultural text without a named human reviewer
metrics.basis: Human oversight expectation; editorial-review exception in the EU text, as a benchmark.
metrics.method: Check review field.

metrics.name: Images with an AI-tool or licence record missing
metrics.basis: Terms let the organizer request image licences and put infringement liability on the participant.
metrics.method: Check register.

metrics.name: Registry codepoints without a glyph in the embedded export fonts
metrics.basis: Font coverage is untested; a person also checks mark placement.
metrics.method: Map codepoints to glyphs per embedded font (fontTools).

modules.method: Each node run writes a W3C PROV-style JSON-LD record: output (entity), node and version (activity), handle or tool (agent), inputs, source ids, human_contribution and decided_by. Setting the VTC entry flag turns on competition-project mode: private, no forks, no gallery or search, handles hidden, public sharing of board images blocked with a warning. Export mode then (a) removes handles, fork authors and author fields from boards, appendix and metadata, keeping the ledger private; (b) embeds the mapped IPTC term and a visible AI label on AI-involved images; (c) keeps Content Credentials off; (d) writes an appendix of AI use, sources, module names and licences; (e) checks glyph coverage; (f) lints source ids, assumption flags, licence records, reviews and visibility. Prompts are hashed in the browser. The gate fails if any rule fails.
visualization: Lineage graph: output to activity to agent, coloured human, AI-assisted or AI-generated (platform view only)
Corner provenance badge on every result card: author type, source count, AI-drafted human-checked state
Export checklist with pass/fail rows, contribution and decision records, and a fix link per failure; false assumptions kept visible
Before-and-after metadata panel: identity fields removed per file, plus any neutral signer or claim-generator text
modules.human_judgment: Whether AI use is appropriate for each element, what each person contributed, accountability for every statement, authorship claims, reading the competition rules and tool terms, and the decision to publish after results.
modules.limits: Labels are declared and lost when platforms strip metadata; a C2PA record does not prove authorship. Brief anonymity clause unread. Whether a private page counts as unpublished is the organizer's decision. EU dates unsettled; Canadian AI copyright unsettled. The mode needs platform-packet support.

modules.name: Cultural-context readiness register, content-keyed review gate and board-statement builder
modules.design_question: Which cultural-context claims can the boards honestly make today, what evidence and Indigenous-review status back each, and what do entrants actually get before 30 Nov 2026?
modules.effort: 5 person-days (the review_state flag in module manifests ships earlier, in core)
inputs: Outputs and gates of M01-M07
Board outline from PRES
Jury criterion text for cultural context (supplied summary until brief confirmed)
Review records (reviewer, scope, date, consent to be named)
Ethics-check record (instructor, BREB answer)
outputs: review_state_register.json (per module, list, card deck and Nation string)
entrant_scope.json (what ships to entrants before 30 Nov)
export_gate_M08 (M01, M05 where released, M07 must pass)

parameters.name: claim
parameters.unit: text with evidence type
parameters.relationship: A claim needs matching evidence (geometry from M06, source from M02 or M04, provenance from M05, status from M01); a claim without it is demoted to intent wording.

parameters.name: criterion_item
parameters.unit: enum City in Nature, cultural-geographic-environmental character, reconciliation and Indigenous perspectives
parameters.relationship: Each criterion item gets a coverage state, not a score: coverage is not quality, and the jury judges quality. Wording shows 'from supplied summary' until the brief is confirmed.

parameters.name: needs_nation_input
parameters.unit: list
parameters.relationship: Items only a Nation can answer stay open and visible, so the boards do not fill the gap with the team's own voice.

parameters.name: review_state
parameters.unit: enum unreviewed prototype, reviewed (scope, reviewer, date), released; keyed to content
parameters.relationship: Any module, list or card that renders a Nation-language string, a cultural prompt card or a cultural phrase list is gated, whatever its category (M06 names and cards, M01 stage B lists, M05 lists). Unreviewed items are hidden from entrants. Stage A ban list is an unreviewed platform rule.

parameters.name: entrant_scope_for_vtc_2026
parameters.unit: fixed statement shown in the tool and on the README
parameters.relationship: Entrants get M01 stage A, M06 geometry (City names only) and M07. CULT cards, lists and Nation strings follow after review, likely after 30 Nov, so the tool must not imply it covers the 30% criterion fully.

parameters.name: reviewer_independence
parameters.unit: declared: not a Nation referral office, not tied to any juror, not a Buildner advisor or in-house juror for VTC 2026, consent to be named
parameters.relationship: A referral office would use the staff time M01 asks entrants to spare; a reviewer tied to a juror or to Buildner's cultural advisors (cl. 10.4) could breach contact rules or conflict. Declared in the record. Team rule.

parameters.name: reviewer_plan
parameters.unit: budget line (amount and source named by the team), contact deadline 28 Oct 2026, written fallback
parameters.relationship: No reviewer, budget or contact exists and registration closes in 8 days. Fallback if no signed-off reviewer by 13 Nov: no CULT content ships for VTC 2026. The deadline is a team assumption.

parameters.name: ethics_check
parameters.unit: record: instructor and UBC BREB answer, date
parameters.relationship: User tests with student teams and Indigenous review may be research with participants. TCPS 2 Art. 2.1 covers course-based activities; Art. 2.5 exempts only assessment testing; Ch. 9 applies if Indigenous people take part. Ask; do not self-classify.

parameters.name: brief_verification
parameters.unit: record: version, date, confirmed weights, criterion text, anonymity wording, site coordinates; deadline 13 Nov
parameters.relationship: The brief is still unopened after two rounds. A registered team member downloads it, so brief-derived values stop depending on a supplied summary.

metrics.method: Join claims with evidence.

metrics.method: Check every module, list and card manifest for review_state.

metrics.method: Check records exist.

modules.method: The node collects state from M01-M07 and builds a three-column register: claim, evidence and source, status (evidenced, intent only, needs Nation input, out of scope). It lists the review_state of every module, list, deck and Nation string, keyed to content; anything unreviewed is hidden from entrants, and course demos carry a prototype ribbon. It records the entrant scope for VTC 2026, the reviewer plan, the ethics check and the brief verification. It generates board text skeletons with mandatory blocks: the per-Nation engagement statement (M01), the AI-use-and-sources appendix (M07), the cultural-material provenance note (M05) and a limits statement. The user rewrites all narrative. The export gate refuses to pass if M01 or M07 fail, or M05 where released. No metric becomes a cultural-quality number.
visualization: Three-column register board (claim, evidence, status) with source and gate chips
Criterion map: three cultural-context items with coverage chips and open-item counts, no totals
Review-state table: module, list or deck, state, reviewer scope and date (name only with consent)
Entrant-scope panel: what ships before 30 Nov; limits box that cannot be removed from the export
modules.human_judgment: Writing the narrative, choosing what to claim, how to describe the relationship to the Nations, who the reviewer is, when to release, and what to ask the instructor and BREB.
modules.limits: A coverage register can be gamed with intent-only wording. Criterion wording comes from a supplied summary. Nothing here predicts a jury result. With no reviewer, budget or contact yet, most CULT content likely stays off until after 30 Nov 2026.
